title: Sleeping Beauty

story_parts.intro: Once upon a time, in a kingdom of rolling Tuscan hills, cypress trees, and olive groves, a king and queen welcomed a baby girl named Aurora. The great hall of their hilltop castle, with its terracotta roofs and bell tower, was filled with frescoes and laughter. In the stone piazza below, the fountain sparkled while villagers danced with tambourines and lutes. Long tables held roast meats, fresh bread, honeyed sweets, and a candied-fruit torta. The king and queen placed baby Aurora in a hand-carved cradle. Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather came in colorful shawls and aprons. They blessed the child with beauty, kindness, and courage. Then the doors flew open. Maleficent stood in dark robes and horns. She cursed Aurora: before the sun set on her sixteenth birthday, she would prick her finger on a spinning wheel spindle and fall into a sleep like death. The fairies opposed her. Merryweather softened the curse: Aurora would not die, but sleep until true love's kiss awakened her. Maleficent vanished, and the kingdom grew quiet.
story_parts.developpement: To keep Aurora safe, Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather hid her in a rustic stone cottage deep in a chestnut and cypress forest. There they raised her as Briar Rose. They baked bread, tended a small garden, and mended clothes by hand. Aurora gathered berries, sang gentle melodies to woodland animals, and shared simple meals of polenta, cheese, and figs. The fairies celebrated each birthday with a small cake and wildflowers. Years passed in golden autumn light. On the morning of her sixteenth birthday, while she was still fifteen until the church bells rang noon, the fairies told her to stay close. But a strange pull led Aurora up the hill to the old castle. In a tower room, she found an old wooden spinning wheel, a relic of the household's weaving past. She touched the spindle. The sharp point pricked her finger. Aurora fell into a deep sleep. The fairies found her, laid her on a bed with wildflowers, and a hush fell over the castle.
story_parts.conclusion: Prince Phillip loved Aurora with all his heart. He rode through the dark woodland of wild blackberry brambles and thorny wild roses that surrounded the hilltop castle. The thorns tore at his cloak, but his courage did not fail. Maleficent rose before him and transformed into a great dragon. Phillip battled her with his sword, and Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather stood as guardians, opposing Maleficent's darkness. At last, Phillip defeated the dragon. He climbed to the tower room and found Aurora asleep. He kissed her gently. True love's kiss broke the curse. Aurora opened her eyes, and the whole kingdom woke with her. Bells rang over the piazza, and everyone celebrated. Kindness, courage, and true love had overcome the darkest curse.

To keep Aurora safe, Flora, Fauna, and Merryweather hid her in a rustic stone cottage deep in a chestnut and cypress forest. There they raised her as Briar Rose. The sharp point pricked her finger. Aurora fell into a deep sleep. The fairies found her, laid her on a bed with wildflowers, and a hush fell over the castle.

Prince Phillip loved Aurora with all his heart. He rode through the dark woodland of wild blackberry brambles and thorny wild roses that surrounded the hilltop castle.
